ordinary_paper_recommendation: QUALIFIED PASS with minor manuscript/source corrections F01-F09 before final clean copy

F01.finding: The generic definition restricts d >= 1 although the source takes the least homogeneous degree. For I=P homogeneous prime, f=1 has (I:1)=P and the source invariant is 0. The printed generic definition instead gives 1 in a polynomial ring with a suitable linear element outside P. Crown J is not prime, so its result is unaffected.
F01.correction: Use d >= 0 (and f nonzero), then retain the crown-specific exclusion of constants in Remark 3.2.

F02.finding: The paired cut T=A union its matched B vertices is V minus {ai,bi,aj,bj}. The text instead says its complements are V minus those four vertices. This reverses the cut and its complement; the displayed Mij ideal is correct.
F02.correction: Replace whose complements are V minus ... by which are T=V minus ..., or say whose complements are {ai,bi,aj,bj}.

F03.finding: The rank-one explanation describes a single determinantal block, but Mij has two disjoint edge blocks. Using one common pair s,u for both blocks would impose extra minors. The cited general completed-component theorem already supplies primality, so no main-proof dependency is missing.
F03.correction: Say each block uses independent rank-one parameters, with independent coordinates for isolated vertices; the resulting disjoint-block quotient embeds in one polynomial ring. Or rely explicitly on [1] for primality.

F04.finding: The sentence says ai and bj belong to Y minus {bi}. The vertex ai is in X. The required containment is nevertheless true because both vertices belong to {ai} union (Y minus {bi}).
F04.correction: Replace since ai and bj in Y minus {bi} lie in the block with since ai and bj lie in {ai} union (Y minus {bi}).

F05.finding: The module identity in the actual frozen crown Lemma 5.7 is cited from its reference [2], Proposition 4.2: Cooper, Seceleanu, Tohuaneanu, Pinto and Villarreal, Generalized minimum distance functions and algebraic invariants of Geramita ideals. It is not cited there from manuscript [7] Mohammadi-Sharifan. That latter reference concerns a different colon lineage; the printed attribution is unsupported by the retained passage.
F05.correction: Say [3, Lemma 5.7] uses the module identity, citing Cooper et al., Proposition 4.2; either add that bibliography entry from the frozen crown reference list or omit the lineage clause. This manuscript proves the identity directly, so no new source retrieval is needed.

F06.severity: minor source-comparison proof gap; no main-theorem impact
F06.finding: A connected dominating set of the star component alone need not contain two leaves: {ai} already dominates that star. The actual [4, Definition 4.6/Theorem 4.15] requires A intersect Vi to dominate G[Vi union T], including deleted vertices. The manuscript omits that constraint while asserting the 3+1 computation.
F06.correction: State the constrained definition. In Q_i, the star-side subset must contain ai to connect/dominate the star, and at least two leaves bj,bk: with only bj, deleted aj is undominated. Two distinct leaves suffice to dominate every deleted al. The isolated bi dominates all deleted al. For Mij each edge requires both endpoints to dominate deleted vertices on both sides. Thus 3+1 and 2+2 are correct.

F07.section: Abstract; strategy; Section 8 preamble; Section 10 provenance
F07.finding: The blanket description of every displayed witness as an explicit construction of [3, Proposition 5.2] is too precise. That proposition handles P0 by the connected-domination equality, without displaying this monomial. The monomial support {a1,a3,b1,b2} is the connected dominating set in [3, Lemma 5.1], and the monomial construction is supplied by [2, Proposition 3.6]. The Ri witness printed here also uses y instead of the x-only source choice, a harmless coordinate symmetry.
F07.correction: Describe the nonempty-cut witnesses as the constructions of [3, Proposition 5.2], up to relabeling/coordinate symmetry; attribute P0 to [3, Lemma 5.1] and the connected-domination construction of [2]. None is new.

F08.finding: A proof-ending square appears after only the first paragraph in each proposition although essential cases follow. Proposition 6.1 also uses xaa/aa where a coordinate pair at an X vertex is intended; membership forces positive vertex degree, not specifically positive x exponent.
F08.correction: Move each square to the actual end of its proof. Say some vertex of X has positive vertex degree. Optionally repair the awkward preimage sentence in Proposition 5.2 by writing sigma(f) satisfies the PX hypothesis, hence sigma(f) in PX and f in PY.

F09.finding: The required radicality in [4, Theorem 3.5] is that of J_G + J_transversal, not radicality of the colon itself. Here (J:P_tau) is an intersection of primes, hence already radical; conflating the two can obscure the actual missing bridge.
F09.correction: Replace radicality hypothesis on the colon with radicality of J_G + J_transversal, whose identification with the colon is the missing equality step.

O01.subject: Exact endpoint
O01.assessment: K arbitrary, integer n>=4, edges ai-bj iff i!=j, S has 4n variables, every cut-point T, exact ideal colon and minimum4. Matches raw369163 and frozen crown Conjecture5.6; neither global minimum alone nor an upper bound.

O02.subject: Radical decomposition and six families
O02.assessment: Actual [1] Cor2.2, Theorem3.2 and Cor3.9 supply arbitrary-field radicality, completed-component primes, and cut criterion. Frozen crown Thm3.3 gives X,Y,X-ai,Y-bi,paired n-2 deletions, plus empty. Q includes ai in the block and isolated bi; M has the two cross edges. Cut sets/linear parts distinguish all families at n>=4. M is one ideal per unordered pair. F02/F03 are exposition repairs, not a missing structural theorem.

O03.subject: Separator iff
O03.assessment: Distribute element colon. Surviving index set cannot be empty. If tau absent, choose g_lambda in P_lambda minus P_tau and multiply; product is outside the prime P_tau but inside the intersection. If tau present, equality forces P_tau subset of every additional intersectand, prohibited by incomparability. Converse is immediate. Works for arbitrary f.

O04.subject: Minimum, zero, constants, module
O04.assessment: Zero gives S. Nonzero constants give J, distinct from every crown minimal prime. Positive-degree convention is equivalent here but not generically: F01. Ideal colon distributes; (P_tau:P_tau)=S, while for lambda!=tau choose a in P_tau minus P_lambda, so ga in P_lambda implies g in P_lambda. Thus (J:P_tau)=intersection of other distinct primes. A nonzero homogeneous quotient class is precisely a separator representative, with the same degree.

O05.subject: Multigrading
O05.assessment: Generators are vertex-homogeneous. A homogeneous ideal generated by such elements contains each multidegree part of any member; summing gives converse. Support cardinality is <= degree even with repeated exponents. A supported deleted vertex divides each monomial through one of its two coordinates, giving automatic target membership. Constants/empty support are included.

O06.subject: Contraction for arbitrary combinations
O06.assessment: Retraction zeroes outside-U coordinates. Every generator maps to itself or zero. Therefore its image ideal is generated by survivors; each survivor is in I intersect S_U, and h in that contraction maps to itself. This proves equality without assuming membership monomial by monomial, without elimination, and with arbitrary coefficients/cancellations.

O07.subject: Full-side support <=2
O07.assessment: For target PX, only pure-Y components remain. All Qi memberships survive componentwise. Support0 or1 gives zero survivor ideal; support2 becomes a singleton after deleting an index in support. Thus h=0, including powers on one/two vertices.

O08.subject: Full-side support3; all-field Gauss step
O08.assessment: Support3 forces degree3 and vertex degree1 each. With U={br,bs,bt}, Qr and Qs contract to principal ideals ([bs,bt]),([br,bt]). In R=K[all U coordinates except x_bs], the coefficients y_bt and -x_bt*y_bs have gcd1. Primitive linear polynomial is irreducible over Frac(R), hence over R by Gauss. Distinct vertex degrees prevent association. S_U is a polynomial UFD; irreducibles are prime, so divisibility by both implies divisibility by their degree4 product. Nonzero multiples have degree>=4 over a domain. Contradiction. No quotient UFD/radicality assumption, no division by2, no field-size assumption.

O09.subject: PY symmetry
O09.assessment: The involution ai<->bi together with x<->y preserves edge-minor ideals (signs immaterial), fixes P0 and each unordered M, and swaps PX/PY,Q/R. Apply it to f to obtain the PX statement, then invert. Thus the same obstruction holds for PY in every field.

O10.subject: Q_i complete support split
O10.assessment: Avoiding X-ai leaves U subset {ai} union Y. Membership PX forces ai degree>0. If bi absent, P0 contracts to D(U), in Q_i. If bi present, <=3 degree leaves either U={ai,bi} or U={ai,bi,bj}. Mij contracts to zero in the former (choose j!=i), and to ([ai,bj]) in the latter. These belong to Q_i. Powers/cancellations covered by the ideal contraction. F04 fixes the printed false set membership.

O12.subject: P0
O12.assessment: PX and PY force nonzero components to meet both sides. Degree<=3 gives a singleton side. If singleton ai, Qi contracts to block minors with endpoints in U, all in D(U) subset P0; singleton bj uses Rj. Zero/constant components already vanish through PX/PY.

O13.subject: Mixed lower bound
O13.assessment: A component outside automatic Mij membership is supported on its four surviving vertices. Both sides occur by PX/PY, and a side is singleton by degree<=3. Singleton ai/aj uses Qi/Qj; singleton bi/bj uses Ri/Rj. Survivor ideal contains only the matching cross minor of Mij, or is zero. Testing primes are distinct from target even at n=4. Hence all components belong to Mij.

O14.subject: P0 quartic
O14.assessment: Support a1,a3,b1,b2 meets each full-side or one-deleted-side cut; a mixed prime retains only two index pairs but the witness uses three. Thus every other prime contains the monomial. y=0,x=t annihilates D(V) and preserves a nonzero monomial. Degree4 and exact colon follow; source attribution refined in F07.

O15.subject: PX and PY quartics
O15.assessment: Two disjoint Y minors are nonzero in the domain S_Y, hence outside L(X), and in P0. For each Qi a disjoint pair avoids i and is in its block. PY and every Ri kill an endpoint of each Y pair. A mixed cut kills a vertex among four distinct Y vertices, hence kills one minor factor. Symmetry gives PY. n=4 suffices.

O16.subject: Q and R quartics
O16.assessment: x_ai*x_bk*[bi,bj], i,j,k distinct: PX,Q_l(l!=i) via x_ai; P0 via minor; PY via Y factor. R_l uses x_bk unless l=k, then both minor endpoints are killed. Mixed cut kills ai or bk; if neither, survivor index pair={i,k}, hence bj is killed. Target specialization kills all Q generators but gives -x_ai*x_bk*x_bj*s !=0 in every field. The combined side/coordinate swap gives exactly the printed y_bi*y_ak*[ai,aj]; its mirrored image is a nonzero monomial as well. Thus no unsupported symmetry/nonmembership assumption.

O17.assessment: [ai,aj]*[bi,bj] is in P0,PX,PY; each Q_l kills an endpoint of the X factor and each R_l an endpoint of Y factor. Every different unordered mixed pair kills ai or aj. Target columns ai,bj=(1,0),aj,bi=(0,1), others0 annihilate both cross minors and deleted coordinates; witness=-1 !=0 even in char2. Exact colon by O03.

O18.assessment: Every target family satisfies (3) for any homogeneous degree<=3 polynomial by summing multigraded components; O03 excludes exact separators. O14-17 produce degree4 exact-colon witnesses for each target. Therefore the set defining the minimum is nonempty and its minimum is4, uniformly in K and n.

O19.subject: New low-degree endpoints
O19.assessment: For 0<=d<=3, any h in the degree-d piece of intersection of other primes belongs to target by proved implication(3), hence J. Reverse inclusion holds in every degree. O04 identifies the entire ideal intersection with (J:P_tau), so both (intersection other primes)_d=J_d and (J:P_tau)_d=J_d hold. This is an ideal-colon assertion; it is not inferred from a single element-colon containment. Negative graded pieces, if intended, are zero by convention.

O20.subject: Bounded prior comparisons
O20.assessment: Frozen crown journal retains all-cuts conjecture, known empty/mixed cases, and quartic upper bounds; copied Q subscripts are indeed present. Older Liwski Def2.3 and Thm4.15 concern two components over C; F06 restores its constrained domination hypothesis. Full sides have n singleton components so are excluded. Thm3.5 equality requires radicality of J+transversal ideal, not automatically of the colon (the colon here is already radical). Newer v2 bound leaves v^-_X=3: outside-X hyperedges Y,Y-bi,Y-{bi,bj}; every pair misses a latter edge, every triple meets all. Hypothesis H fails for every nonempty crown cut. Generalized Setting4.1/Thm4.12 requires closed graphs; three independent Y neighbors of ai form an induced claw, impossible under a closed interval-clique labeling. No complete subsumption bridge follows. F05/F07 repair provenance wording.
